coach.responsibility: Read the objective for what is to be improved: which positions of which world, given to you to read, have their workers improved (one or several together), what the incumbent workers are (`config show` on that world), how a task is judged if the objective says, and the budget. Set what this round improves first, keep every position working toward it, and give the task-setting position the aspects its tasks have to show. Collect the problems the diagnosis places in the target world or its positions rather than in a worker, and report them, with their evidence, as part of the delivery for the target world's maintainer; they are not a difference between workers.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

task-setter.responsibility: Find the tasks the target positions do: moments in the target world's checkpoints and records (`checkpoints`, `monitor`) where a target position owes work, from which a world continued at that checkpoint makes the task; and, where they show something those moments do not, small tasks you make to the position's contract. Write for each task its starting point, what is asked of the position, and how its result is judged: the judging the objective gives, or one you propose, with why it tells a better result from a worse one. Publish them as diagnostic tasks, a release of your repository, for the positions that run and diagnose the worker. The held-out tasks the evaluation measures on are not yours: another position brings them, and you do not see them.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

sparring-partner.responsibility: Run the worker you are given on the diagnostic tasks, as a user runs a world: for each task, continue the target world, or the world the task names, at the task's checkpoint into a world of your own (`continue <world> --checkpoint NAME --config FILE`), with a configuration that changes only the target positions' workers and keeps the rest as the target world has it (its other workers and its resources, which `config show` gives), and drive it as far as the task asks. Keep the records of every run: which worker, which task, which repetition, the world, its receipts, its time stream (`monitor`) and what it produced (`artifacts`), and push them to your repository for the positions that diagnose and change the worker. When the evaluation keeps a worker, put it back into the target world: continue its latest round with that worker into the next round and drive it, from a point where the positions the worker is put into still owe work; that round is the newest run, and its records go the same way. A put-back has run only when its records show the kept worker doing that work. You record what happened; you do not judge why.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

diagnostician.responsibility: Read the records of the runs and find what the worker does badly on the tasks and why, each finding pointing to the turn, step or output in the records that shows it: for example a neighbor's output not read, a tool used wrongly, a requirement lost after the context was compacted, or a model too weak for the task. Place each problem in its layer first: a world that did not supply what the work needs, did not say what the worker had to know, or a position whose text contradicts itself, is not a worker's problem; send those to the direction owner, with their evidence, and leave them out of any difference between workers. Read the results themselves against the judging the tasks name, citing their lines, not only their scores. Name a worker's problem by what can change it: the agent, the model, its effort, the agent's own settings, a skill, the worker's own prompt or its assets. When a candidate has done the diagnostic tasks, compare it with the incumbent and say what is left.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

tuner.responsibility: Make candidate workers from the diagnosis, changing only the worker: the agent, the model, its effort, the agent's own settings, skills, the worker's own prompt and assets. The positions' function text, contracts and everything else of the target world stay as they are. A candidate may start from any worker already tried, the incumbent included. Your repository root is the delivery: the workers the target world uses as they are, as its configuration of the target positions, with what each candidate changed and why. Hand each candidate to the runs position to try on the diagnostic tasks, and change it again from what the diagnosis finds. You do not see the held-out tasks, and you do not try to guess them.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

judge.responsibility: Settle the judging of the held-out tasks with the position that brings them as a user of the improved workers, and check that the judging tells the incumbent from a candidate. Evaluate independently and blind: that position runs every held-out task for the incumbent and the candidate from the same starting point with the same judging, and gives you each result under a label that does not tell whose it is. It reads no other position's repository, so name to it, in an issue in its repository, the workers of each candidate to run. Judge every result on its own, from that result alone and read in full, without comparing it with another result before every judgement is pushed, and write with each judgement what in that result it rests on. A judgement made once you knew whose result it was, or produced by a script instead of by judging that result, does not count. When every judgement is pushed and the labels are published, measure the difference between the workers and its spread. Keep the evaluation record: which tasks, how many runs of each worker, every judgement, the difference, which workers stay and why. Each version is approved by another position, which reads your record: the delivered workers must be those this objective's evaluation keeps and the round they were put back into for this objective must have run; a record or a round carried over from an earlier objective does not count. When no candidate does better than the incumbent, the delivered workers are the incumbent's and the record says so. A run that ended without a verified release is `failed`, not measured, and the record says how the comparison counts it. Never put a held-out task in an issue, a comment or your wiki, which positions that do not read your code also read.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

referee.responsibility: Approve each version, as the position that sets no task, judges no result, runs no worker and changes none: check that the delivered workers are those the evaluation keeps, that their configuration runs in the target world as it is, and that the round they were put back into ran with them, from the records themselves. Read the evaluation record and the results it rests on as they are, and the feedback of the position that uses each version, and approve only what they support; the last version you approve releases the world.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

trial-user.responsibility: Use the improved workers as someone who needs the target positions' work done would: bring work of your own that the target positions do, the held-out tasks, which the positions that improve the worker never see. Before any version is approved, try the incumbent workers and each candidate's workers on it; you read no other position's repository, so the judging position names each candidate's workers in an issue in your repository. A version is approved on that judging, so it comes after your runs: do not wait for one. Keep your tasks and everything that says which worker did what in your repository's files, never in an issue, a release, your wiki or a comment, which positions that must not see them read. Hand each result to the judging position under a label that does not tell which worker made it, and keep which is which until every result is judged. Once a version is released in `world/result`, use its workers on work of your own and report your experience as issues in your own repository, one point an issue, without revealing a task: what it did well or badly on your work compared with the incumbent. You see the candidates and the versions, not how they were made.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact
